summary.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, data centre demand and utilisation targets, but evasive on the Rs.500 crore fund raise, the Rs.120 crore UAE order, the Q4 non-fin-and-tube share and the specific data centre order book. Several answers were vague or deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: Yes, even I can say next eight quarters will be highest ever. So, this quarter also will be average but number I cannot disclose.
So, now we have eight new businesses, so that is also we have to build the inventory.
Of course, slight improvement will be there, but honestly in the last two, three weeks in this copper and aluminum silver price is beyond the expectation because they sharply increase.
